凜 りん — dignified; bracing cold

凜 describes a dignified, firmly composed bearing, or cold that feels sharp and bracing. It can also describe a clear, ringing voice or sound. Learn the constructions 凜と and 凜とした + noun, rather than adding な as if this were an ordinary な-adjective.
凜とした声がひびく。 (りんとしたこえがひびく。) — A clear, firm voice rings out.
凜とした朝の寒気 (りんとしたあさのかんき) — The bracing chill of the morning.

These short examples come from Daijisen. The second is a noun phrase, not a complete sentence. In both, とした describes the following noun; it does not necessarily report an earlier change into that state. 凜と can modify an action. JMdict labels the word a taru adjective and an adverb taking と; that classification does not make 凜 an い-adjective.

This is a single-character Sino-Japanese word, not a compound. 凜 supplies the whole on reading リン and the dignity/coldness meaning. JMdict also recognizes 凛 (りん) in the same lexical family. The variant spelling does not introduce another pronunciation or word.

寒い (さむい) is the broader everyday adjective for cold weather or surroundings. 凜とした adds the sharp, bracing quality in the morning example; it is not a neutral substitute for every occurrence of 寒い. 厳しい (きびしい) can describe severe cold, but also strict standards and harsh circumstances; do not transfer all those uses to 凜.

澄む (すむ) overlaps for a clear, resonant voice. 冷静 (れいせい) emphasizes mental composure and clear-headedness, not necessarily the dignified outward bearing conveyed by 凜とした. Warmth contrasts with the cold sense, but is not an opposite of dignity.

A 凜とした声 can sound clear and firm without being loud, angry or cruel. Likewise, a dignified manner does not establish someone's social rank or moral superiority. Select the translation from what is being described.

The full dictionary family also records a tense atmosphere sense. This article focuses on bearing, sound and bracing cold; it is not an exhaustive account of every literary or historical construction. Neither dictionary inclusion nor the variant spelling establishes a frequency ranking. Personal-name usage is outside this article's scope.
